messages:
maria: Hey team — quick follow-up from the gateway sync: I'm calling this 'ingress terminalization' which is the point where the edge decides a streaming request is effectively finished (either success, client abort, or switched to fallback). Need to pick an owner for the terminalization contract and clarify retry/hedge semantics.

jonathan: +1 on naming. Can you sketch the failure modes you want the contract to cover?

maria: Sure. Rough list: 1) upstream backend returns final trailer and closes 2) client cancels in-flight 3) network drop between edge->backend but client still attached 4) backend stalls/slow and we hedge to another replica 5) partial response that must be resumable vs non-resumable 6) quota/backpressure triggered mid-stream.

lee: For (3) and (4) we need to decide who owns replays/resume tokens. Do we make edge responsible for checkpointing K/V token snapshots or push that to the backend protocol?

sam: My preference: edge owns ephemeral resume checkpoints for short-term hedging only (ms->secs). Persistent checkpoints that survive full backend restart should be a backend responsibility. Edge checkpoints should be lightweight (token index + small hash).

jonathan: That aligns with runtime cost goals. But it means edge must expose a clear API to backends: Status(stream_id) -> {cursor, window, maybe-opaque}. Also need bounds: how many checkpoints per request? evict policy?

maria: Proposal A (edge-owned short-term): edge keeps an in-memory sliding window of checkpoints sized by token-count and time; hedging/fast-fail use these to resume or replay to a cold replica. On catastrophic failure, we fall back to full request replay (if idempotent) or return partial+error.

maria: Proposal B (backend-assisted resumability): backends publish a resumable token in trailers; edge persists that token to cloudstore for longer TTLs. Edge still ephemeral-checkpoints for micro-hedge.

lee: Tradeoffs: A is simpler for latency (no external write on hot path) but puts memory pressure and complex eviction logic at edge. B adds persistence cost and latency on finalization but supports stronger resumability.

sam: Also need to decide retry/hedge semantics when client is streaming data upstream (like file-upload or streaming audio). If we re-route to another backend mid-stream, we lose in-flight upstream data unless client or edge buffers it. Buffering at edge is expensive and risky.

jonathan: So we should codify: if request has streaming request-body (client->edge->backend) we only permit hedging for short periods where edge can replay input (e.g., small buffers) OR we require client to support resume tokens in client protocol. Otherwise, no transparent midflight failover. Document this clearly.

maria: Another question: trailer semantics on abort vs success. Should edge synthesize a trailer when it aborts a request because of capacity/budget? Currently some clients expect trailers with structured error metadata.

lee: We should standardize on a minimal handshake: trailers include status_code, resume_token (optional), checkpoint_cursor (optional), and a terminal_reason string. If edge aborts and has no resume token -> send terminal_reason=EDGE_ABORT_NO_RESUME.

sam: Also include a boolean in the header that signals whether the response is resumable at all: X-Stream-Resumable: true/false. That will avoid clients assuming resumability.

maria: Good call. We also need to protect memory/connection slots: when hedging, do hedged requests consume full capacity quotas? We should charge hedged copies to the same budget but mark them as hedged so billing and throttling can account.

jonathan: Agreed — mark hedged attempts with metadata (hedge_id, primary_preempted boolean). This is important for the autoscaler metrics and billing transparency.

lee: One more long-term thought: if we move to a model where backends are using a unified streaming protocol (gRPC+resume extension), many of these problems move to protocol-level agreements and the gateway simplifies. But transition is nontrivial.

maria: OK action items from this thread: 
- jonathan: draft a 1-page contract for ingress terminalization with fields: terminal_reason enums, resume_token shape, checkpoint_cursor shape, X-Stream-Resumable header semantics, and hedging metadata. Due EOD Fri.
- lee: prototype a memory budget model for in-edge checkpoint sliding window and eviction policy. Keep numbers and worst-case RPS analysis. Due Tue.
- sam: list SDK client changes needed for client-side resume support and proposed header names. Due Mon.
- i'll collect and fold into a short RFC for the gateway docs.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: new branch created: feature/ingress-terminalization-contract by maria. CI queued.

jonathan: I'll start the contract doc. Quick question — do we want to allow user-configurable resume TTLs per route? Some customers will prefer longer TTLs for reliability.

maria: Yes but default must be short (30s) to avoid unbounded storage. Route-level override with org policy and chargeback. Note in RFC.

sam: if anyone's blocked on examples, I have a small test harness that simulates streaming hedges and client aborts. Happy to share.

maria: Great. Thanks all. If no objections I'll mark this for RFC intake next week.

jonathan: No objections from me. :+1:

lee: Sounds good. :thumbsup:

maria: End thread — moving to RFC tracker.
